subject: general
question: When an acid reacts with a reactive metal, the products formed are:

options.text: A metal oxide and nitrogen gas evolve
A salt and carbon dioxide gas form
An alkali and hydrogen peroxide form
A salt and hydrogen gas are produced

solution:
The correct answer is __**A salt and hydrogen gas are produced**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **reactive metal** reacts with a dilute **acid**, it undergoes a **chemical reaction** that results in the formation of a **metal salt** and the evolution of **hydrogen gas**.
 
• This interaction is typically a **displacement reaction**, where the **metal**, being more **reactive**, displaces the **hydrogen** atoms from the **acid** molecule.
 
• The general **chemical equation** for this reaction can be represented as: **Metal + Dilute Acid → Metal Salt + Hydrogen Gas**.
 
• The **salt** formed during this process depends on the specific **metal** and the type of **acid** used in the **reaction**. For instance, **Hydrochloric acid** produces **chlorides**, while **Sulfuric acid** produces **sulfates**.
 
• The rate of this **reaction** depends on the position of the **metal** in the **reactivity series**; metals higher in the series react more **vigorously** than those lower down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Testing for Hydrogen Gas**:
 
 
• The **hydrogen gas** evolved during the **reaction** can be identified using the **Pop Sound Test**.
 
• When a burning **splinter** or **candle** is brought near the mouth of the test tube containing the gas, it burns with a characteristic **pop sound**, confirming the presence of **Hydrogen**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of the Reaction**:
 
 
• **Zinc and Hydrochloric Acid**: When **Zinc (Zn)** granules react with dilute **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, they produce **Zinc chloride (ZnCl2)** and **Hydrogen gas (H2)**.
 
• **Magnesium and Sulfuric Acid**: The **reaction** between **Magnesium (Mg)** and dilute **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** yields **Magnesium sulfate (MgSO4)** and **Hydrogen gas**.
 
 
 
• **Exception with Nitric Acid**:
 
 
• Generally, when a **metal** reacts with **Nitric acid (HNO3)**, **hydrogen gas** is **not** evolved.
 
• This is because **Nitric acid** is a very strong **oxidizing agent**. It oxidizes the **hydrogen** produced into **water (H2O)** and itself gets reduced to **nitrogen oxides** like **N2O, NO, or NO2**.
 
• However, **Magnesium (Mg)** and **Manganese (Mn)** are exceptions as they can react with very dilute **Nitric acid** to evolve **hydrogen gas**.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity of Metals**:
 
 
• Metals like **Sodium (Na)** and **Potassium (K)** react **explosively** even with dilute acids due to their high **reactivity**.
 
• Metals like **Copper (Cu)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**, which are below **hydrogen** in the **reactivity series**, do not react with dilute **acids** to produce **hydrogen gas** under normal conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **concentration** of the **acid** and the **surface area** of the **metal** (e.g., powder vs. granules) significantly affect the **speed of the reaction**.
 
• In **industrial applications**, these **reactions** are utilized for the **preparation of hydrogen gas** and various **metallic salts** used in **manufacturing** and **laboratories**.
 
• During the **reaction**, the **temperature** of the solution usually rises, indicating that the **reaction** is **exothermic** in nature.
